## Fork importance {#the-outcome-fork-carries-half-of-everything}

```{r}
#| label: fork-importance
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
# Two readings of each decision on the curve (data/spec_curve_forks.csv): the
# share of the variance of the claim-aligned partial r that its main effect
# carries, and the share of pairs, differing only in that decision, whose two
# members fall in different classes under the bootstrap. Ordered by the share
# of the variance; the estimator in orange, the interactions in grey.
fk <- curve_forks |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    name     = axis_names[axis],
    share    = share / 100,
    crossing = crossing_rate / 100,
    fill     = dplyr::case_when(axis == "estimator" ~ "lead",
                                axis == "interactions" ~ "rest",
                                .default = "axis")
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::if_else(axis == "interactions", -Inf, share)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(name = factor(name, levels = name))
fk_fill <- scale_fill_manual(values = c(lead = orange, axis = ncl_blue, rest = grey_mid),
                             guide = "none")
p_share <- ggplot(fk, aes(share, name, fill = fill)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = fmt_pct(share)), hjust = -0.15, colour = ncl_blue,
            fontface = "bold", size = 4.4) +
  fk_fill +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.55), labels = NULL) +
  labs(x = "share of the variance", y = NULL) +
  theme_slide(15)
p_cross <- ggplot(dplyr::filter(fk, axis != "interactions"), aes(crossing, name, fill = fill)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = fmt_pct(crossing)), hjust = -0.15, colour = ncl_blue,
            fontface = "bold", size = 4.4) +
  fk_fill +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.72), labels = NULL) +
  labs(x = "pairs that change class when it moves alone", y = NULL) +
  theme_slide(15) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
p_share + p_cross
```

::: {.small}
- The **estimator** carries **`r fmt_pct(fork_of("estimator"))`** of the variance, the predictor `r fmt_pct(fork_of("predictor"))` and the outcome `r fmt_pct(fork_of("outcome"))`; the no-opinion rule, the series, the form and the cell weighting together carry `r fmt_pct(sum(purrr::map_dbl(c("noop", "measure", "pred_form", "cell_weight"), fork_of)))`
- The no-opinion rule carries almost none of the variance and still changes the class of `r fmt_pct(fork_of("noop", "crossing_rate"))` of its pairs
:::

::: {.src}
data/spec_curve_forks.csv: main-effect shares of the variance over the curve, and class changes under the wild cluster bootstrap. The [decision map]({{< var site-url >}}exercise/estimand-dial.html) shows where each decision is made.
:::

::: notes
The estimator accounts for the largest share of the variation on the curve, about forty-one per cent, and the predictor comes next at seventeen. The outcome scale, which many people bet on, carries nine. The estimator here is the choice between two estimands, with or without the year effects that remove what all member states went through together, which is why it does so much. The decisions about measurement that occupy so much of the methods literature – how to treat respondents who mention nothing, which published series, whether cells are weighted – carry about one per cent between them, and the interactions, combinations of decisions that matter beyond any single one, about a quarter. Now the right-hand panel, which asks a different question: how often does moving one decision, with everything else held, change whether a specification clears the bootstrap? The estimator and the predictor still lead. But the no-opinion rule, with almost no share of the variance, changes the class of about one pair in twelve. A decision can matter little across the curve and still decide whether your own result is significant. Whoever guessed the estimator in the chat: take the point.
:::

## The reference results in the curve {#the-unit-of-analysis-does-the-work}

```{r}
#| label: analyst-placement
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.2
# The six reference results (data/reference_marks.csv) under three
# conversions of the same statistic: on the degrees of freedom of its own
# inference, where the mark is placed; on the 233 df of the two-way design,
# the common denominator of the conversion lesson; and as Multi100 recorded
# it, drawn only where it differs from the placement, which is PRL47 alone (OA
# has no recorded value). The bands behind are the curve: its full range, its
# middle half and its median (dashed).
conv <- ref_marks |>
  dplyr::select(tag, placed = r_placement, on_233 = r_233, recorded = r_recorded) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(on_233, recorded), names_to = "kind", values_to = "r") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(r), kind != "recorded" | abs(r - placed) > 0.001) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::distinct(ref_marks, tag, r = r_placement) |>
                     dplyr::mutate(kind = "placed")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(kind = factor(kind, levels = c("placed", "on_233", "recorded"),
                              labels = c("own df (placed)", "233 df", "as recorded by Multi100, where it differs")))
row_levels <- rev(ref_marks$tag)
curve_q <- stats::quantile(spec_curve$r_ca, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
ggplot(conv, aes(r, factor(tag, levels = row_levels))) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = min(spec_curve$r_ca), xmax = max(spec_curve$r_ca),
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = plain, alpha = 0.06) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = curve_q[[1]], xmax = curve_q[[3]],
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = plain, alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = curve_q[[2]], colour = plain, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = grey_mid, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = kind, colour = kind), size = 4.2, stroke = 1.1) +
  geom_text(data = ref_marks, aes(x = 0.14, y = tag,
                                  label = sprintf("%d of %d further below zero", rank, nrow(spec_curve))),
            hjust = 0, size = 4, colour = grey_mid, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 1, 4), name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(ink, ink, d_red), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.62, 0.52), breaks = seq(-0.6, 0, by = 0.2),
                     labels = \(x) fmt_num(x, 1)) +
  labs(x = "partial correlation r", y = NULL) +
  theme_slide(15) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left")
```

::: {.small}
- On its own df PRL47 sits beside the original study; Multi100 recorded it at `r fmt_num(mark_of("PRL47", "r_recorded"))`, converted on `r fmt_n(analysts5$n[analysts5$analyst_id == "PRL47"])` respondents
- On 233 df every other result moves, and KEVF1 changes places with KQXUE: the common denominator is a teaching device, worked through in the [conversion lesson]({{< var site-url >}}case/index.html#sec-recorded) of the case study
:::

::: {.src}
data/reference_marks.csv; each statistic converted as $r = t/\sqrt{t^2 + df}$. The bands are the curve: its range, its middle half and its median.
:::

::: notes
Here are the six reference results again, now with the three numbers that each of them could be given. The filled dot is where each sits on the degrees of freedom of its own inference, which is where the curve slide before the bet placed it. The open circle converts the same statistic on two hundred and thirty-three degrees of freedom, the residual degrees of freedom of my own two-way design, which is the common denominator that the conversion lesson uses. The red cross marks the value that Multi100 recorded where it differs from the placement, which happens only for PRL47, whose z was converted on the number of respondents. The bands behind the dots show the curve: its full range, its middle half and its median. Two things to take away. The choice of degrees of freedom moves a result by as much as the largest decisions on the menu do, and the right choice is the one that counts the units that carry the evidence. And once that is done, the five analysts are spread across most of the curve rather than across two orders of magnitude.
:::

## Sign changes by option {#the-sign-flips-are-patterned-not-random}

```{r}
#| label: sign-flips
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.9
# The share of pairs whose two members lie on different sides of zero: for the
# decisions on the curve, pairs that differ only in that decision
# (data/spec_curve_forks.csv); for the options off the curve, each curve
# specification against its twin with the option swapped in
# (data/menu_deviations.csv; the rate repeats the count and is left out).
# Only decisions and options that change at least one sign are drawn.
opt_labels <- menu_opts |> dplyr::select(axis, option, label)
flips <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  curve_forks |>
    dplyr::filter(axis != "interactions") |>
    dplyr::transmute(label = axis_names[axis], sign_changes = sign_changes / 100,
                     where = "decisions on the curve"),
  deviations |>
    dplyr::filter(!on_curve, axis != "se", n_pairs > 0, rule != "identical_to_count") |>
    dplyr::distinct(axis, option, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::left_join(opt_labels, by = c("axis", "option")) |>
    dplyr::transmute(label, sign_changes = sign_changes / 100,
                     where = "options off the curve")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(sign_changes > 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(sign_changes) |>
  dplyr::mutate(label = factor(label, levels = unique(label)))
ggplot(flips, aes(sign_changes, label, fill = where)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = fmt_pct(sign_changes)), hjust = -0.15, colour = ncl_blue,
            fontface = "bold", size = 4.2) +
  facet_grid(where ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`decisions on the curve` = ncl_blue,
                               `options off the curve` = d_red), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.6), labels = NULL) +
  labs(x = "pairs whose two members lie on different sides of zero", y = NULL) +
  theme_slide(14) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, colour = ncl_blue, face = "bold"))
```

::: {.small}
- On the curve, `r sum(spec_curve$r_ca > 0)` of the `r fmt_n(nrow(spec_curve))` specifications lie above zero, all of them GDP growth on the cosmopolitan scale, and `r if (any(spec_curve$r_ca > 0 & spec_curve$sig)) "some" else "none"` with bootstrap p < 0.05
- Off the curve the sign changes come from options that change the question: **pooled OLS** brings in the comparison between countries, and the samples **without the bailout countries** or **before the crisis** remove the cases that the claim is about
:::

::: {.src}
data/spec_curve_forks.csv and data/menu_deviations.csv. The [decision map]({{< var site-url >}}exercise/estimand-dial.html) gives the reason for each option, on the curve or off it.
:::

::: notes
The curve can also be read for where the signs change. On the curve itself there is little to read: sixteen of the eight hundred and sixty-four specifications lie above zero, all of them growth on the cosmopolitan scale, and none of them clears the bootstrap. The estimator, which moves the estimates most, changes no signs at all. The sign changes come from options that the audit moved off the curve, and they are patterned. Swap pooled OLS into every specification and half of them change sign, because pooled OLS lets in the comparison between countries, where the association runs the other way. Leave out the bailout countries, or keep only the years before the crisis, and about a quarter change sign, because those samples remove the cases that the claim is most about. So when this claim flips, it flips for reasons that can be named, and each of those options answers another question, which is why it is taught beside the curve rather than on it.
:::
